page: Amazon Web Services c8g.48xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by 64-bit ARM architecture. The host contains 192 dedicated physical cores and 192 vCPUs running AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 silicon at 2.7 GHz. The system provides 384 GB of system memory, matching a standard compute-oriented ratio of 2 GB per core. The instance includes 50 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, operates without hardware graphics accelerators, and provisions zero local instance storage, requiring network-attached volumes for persistent data.

Benchmark data reflects strong parallel processing scaling across its 192 non-hyperthreaded cores. Multi-threaded stress-ng throughput places in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems, alongside high scores in multi-core Clang compilation and ray tracing. Memory throughput is also strong, achieving uncached read rates exceeding 907 GB/s and write rates over 403 GB/s. In contrast, single-core execution metrics across stress-ng and Geekbench sit in the middle 50 percent, highlighting that peak performance depends on parallel multi-process or multi-threaded distribution rather than raw per-thread instruction speeds.

In operational benchmarks, the instance demonstrates top-tier capabilities in Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput, alongside top-tier database transaction results in PassMark. While prompt processing for smaller language models trails into lower percentiles due to the lack of dedicated vector or matrix extensions and discrete accelerators, its density of dedicated physical cores yields reliable multi-tenant web serving, large-scale code builds, distributed CI/CD execution, and high-concurrency batch processing workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services c8g.48xlarge is a high-density, compute-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with 64-bit ARM architecture. Equipped with 192 physical cores and 192 vCPUs across AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processors at 2.7 GHz, it provides 384 GB of system memory and 50 Gbps of baseline networking. The instance features no discrete GPUs and relies entirely on external storage, having no bundled local disks. Benchmark results show top-tier multi-threaded execution, memory throughput, and high-concurrency performance across Clang software builds, Redis SET operations, and static web serving. While single-thread speeds and localized AI inference operations show moderate baseline throughput, the massive non-hyperthreaded core count delivers consistent compute density. Amazon Web Services c8g.48xlarge is primarily suited for large-scale multi-threaded compiling, high-concurrency microservices, CI/CD runners, and distributed batch computing workloads.
